items.title: 'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
items.summary:
'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
- Published
Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another
items.text:
'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
- Published
Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another disappointing defeat?
The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's first match in charge of United got off to a dreadful start as they had defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute and were 2-0 down by the 13th minute.
That left them with a mountain to climb, with Liverpool scoring twice more in the second half to secure a 4-0 win that kept United second from bottom in the table.
"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino of the situation that faced his new side after those disastrous opening 13 minutes.
"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?
"We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing room."
'Do you down tools and throw the towel in?'
Pochettino certainly does have a point.
Trying to win any game when reduced to 10 men in the first half is difficult. In the entire history of the Premier League Manchester United have managed it on four occasions - each of those at Old Trafford.
Indeed, in the 509 instances of a team receiving one or more red cards in the first half of a Premier League match, they have gone on to win just 88 times.
At Anfield it gets even more difficult, with Arsenal the only team to have beaten Liverpool on their own ground after a first-half dismissal.
For ex-Manchester United captain Roy Keane, though, there are ways to lose if you have a man sent off - and a 4-0 defeat was not one of them.
Speaking before Pochettino's comments, he told Sky Sports: "Are you telling me they couldn't have done better? They lose 4-0 and everyone is saying it's not too bad.
"Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality. I can't believe what I'm hearing from people who have played for the club saying 4-0 is not too bad."
Keane was responding to his former team-mate Gary Neville, who was part of the commentary team for Sky Sports.
"That's where we've got to, where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as though it's just the norm and what should be accepted," said Neville in the closing stages of the game. "The club's standards have dropped so far it's incredible."
The former England full-back added: "There'll be an element of, 'let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off, we've got 10 men and all that sort of stuff', but it rides into the game in midweek and from a defensive perspective I've never seen anything like this."
Keane did not agree with that view as he said: "Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. Unbelievable chances they had and everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad.
"I feel like swearing. I'll try not to. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? Just because they went down to 10 men. That obviously made it a lot more difficult, but if you go down to 10 men is that it? Do you down tools and throw the towel in?"
'I've never seen anything like this' - defeat provides more defensive concern
Despite Keane's comments, a 4-0 loss at Anfield isn't unthinkable - certainly better than losing 7-0 as United did three years ago.
But in the wider context it provides more concern about a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe's top five leagues.
No other team in the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Ligue 1 or Serie A has conceded more than United's 34 goals in all competitions so far this season.
It is also the second successive game they have conceded four goals, while in their last six games in all competitions they have conceded 19.
"I don't think Mauricio Pochettino can write this off," said ex-Leeds and Spurs goalkeeper Paul Robinson on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He has to learn from it. He will have learned about his players and their attitude.
"Liverpool had 27 shots in that game. There were mitigating circumstances early in the game... but why did we get to those circumstances?
"It was because defenders were out of position again. The long ball over the top that catches Matthijs de Ligt out, the lack of communication, the tackle Leny Yoro makes and the defenders being caught out."

items.title: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
items.summary:
Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
Parties remain split on who will lead the next government and whether far right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir will join.
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to fo
items.text:
Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
Parties remain split on who will lead the next government and whether far right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir will join.
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.
Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.
The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.
In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.
Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.
Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.
However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.
If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

items.title: ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card in Anfield humiliation
items.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino argued that Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off and that Manchester United were earlier denied a penalty against Liverpool after suffering the joint-heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history.
Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 win ensured Pochettino equalled Lal Hilditch’s unwanted record fro
items.text:
Mauricio Pochettino argued that Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off and that Manchester United were earlier denied a penalty against Liverpool after suffering the joint-heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history.
Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 win ensured Pochettino equalled Lal Hilditch’s unwanted record from 1926 of losing his first United game by such a scoreline. United’s 34 goals conceded across all competitions this season are the most by any team in European football’s top five leagues.
United were reduced to 10 men after only eight minutes when Yoro was shown a straight red card for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. “He was clearly the last man and it was clearly a foul,” said the Liverpool head coach, Andoni Iraola.
Yet Pochettino took a fiercely opposing view, claiming Isak had waited for contact to be made after losing possession and insisting United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the free-kick that resulted from Yoro’s foul and Liverpool were coasting at 2-0 after only 14 minutes. United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree [it was a red-card offence] because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control.
“Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul. But two minutes before, Jacquet and Mbeumo, how can you compare the situation?
“It is painful for me and for them but we played for more than 80 minutes at Anfield with 10 men. You can be critical of the team, but it’s a penalty for Mbeumo. We can make a mistake and we were punished. They can make a mistake and they were not punished.”
Pochettino defended his decision to give Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 12 months despite the centre-back having a torrid time against Liverpool’s forward line. He also claimed United showed the resolve necessary to drag themselves out of relegation trouble despite being comprehensively outplayed.
“We need to accept the reality and we need to be united,” he said. “It is clear what happened.
“After eight minutes the plan was in the bin, but what I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games.
“Today was a test that for me is very positive. Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more. We are in a situation that is very complicated and difficult, but we fight, we make the effort.”
Rio Ngumoha became the youngest goalscorer in the fixture’s Premier League history and produced a scintillating display alongside the equally impressive Florian Wirtz. Iraola said of the teenager: “He is playing a lot of minutes, on the left and the right, and he is getting used to going outside or cutting inside to finish. I’m happy with the way he arrived in the box to score. The same with Flo. We want them to be more of a threat in the box.”
Iraola recreated Jürgen Klopp’s post-match celebration after the final whistle and fist-pumped the Kop. He said: “Obviously I enjoyed the moment. I still think we owe the fans because they have been very supportive and we’ve had much better results away from home than at home. This is a big game for everyone in the club and we wanted to give them a big win.”

items.summary:
Turkey: Thousands protest closure of critical media outlets
November 22, 2026
Several thousand people in Istanbul took to the streets on Sunday to protest the closure of several opposition-linked media outlets in Turkey.
Protesters chanted, cheered, and whistled as they marched several kilometers th
items.text:
Turkey: Thousands protest closure of critical media outlets
November 22, 2026
Several thousand people in Istanbul took to the streets on Sunday to protest the closure of several opposition-linked media outlets in Turkey.
Protesters chanted, cheered, and whistled as they marched several kilometers through the city, calling for press freedom and freedom of expression.
They carried a huge banner that read: "We want freedom of thought, freedom of the press, and freedom for journalists." The protesters were also carrying placards that read, "The press cannot be silenced."
What sparked the protests?
Turkey's main opposition party, Yeni Parti, called for a protest just days after police raided Sozcu TV, one of the last opposition-aligned television channels.
Senior staff members were arrested during the raid. A government-appointed trustee was installed, and the TV company was placed under compulsory administration.
It was the third takeover in a year following similar actions against Tele1, Halk TV, Turkey's most-watched news channel, and the leading digital news website, T24.
Timur Soykan, a journalist who was briefly detained for criticizing the government, said that the government was doing everything in its power to silence journalists but was failing to do so.
Soykan asked the public to support Halk TV journalists, who plan to continue broadcasting on a new YouTube channel.
Increasing crackdown on critical media in Turkey
Over the past decade, press freedom has faced sustained pressure in the form of prosecutions, digital censorship, and government accusations that journalists are spreading "fake news."
In the last two months alone, Turkey has arrested several journalists for their reporting on a multibillion-dollar investment fund scandal. At least two of the journalists remain in pretrial detention.
According to the media rights group MLSA, twenty-five journalists are currently imprisoned in Turkey.
This year, Reporters Without Borders ranked Turkey 163rd out of 180 countries in its Press Freedom Index.

Jamaica bounced back from losing their opening match to level the four-Test series against the Vitality Roses; England will travel to Jamaica to play further matches on December 5 and 6, as preparation continues for next year's Netball World Cup
Sunday 22 November 2026 21:52, UK
England failed to extend their lead in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series with Jamaica, as the visitors claimed a dominant 55-40 win at the Copper Box Arena.
A day on from a dramatic 47-46 victory in the series opener at the same London venue, England were second-best as the Sunshine Girls claimed a comfortable victory and levelled the four-Test series.
The visitors scored six consecutive points on their way to opening a 15-7 advantage after the first quarter, then the Commonwealth Games silver medallists extended their lead to 11 points by half-time.

A tight third quarter saw Jamaica edge further ahead, with the Sunshine Girls never relinquishing their advantage as they closed out a convincing win on away soil.
"We expected Jamaica to come out hard and they certainly did deliver on that," England coach Anna Stembridge admitted.

items.title: Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
items.summary:
Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism.” Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, w
items.text:
Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism.” Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of "Jewish terrorism" from the man trying to form an Israeli government.
The attacks, the latest in an escalation that began after Hamas launched attacks on Israel from the Gaza Strip in 2023, come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.
Reuters saw burned-out Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans such as "Revenge" and "Death to Arabs" in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately claimed responsibility and no injuries were reported.
Eisenkot called the attacks "Jewish terrorism", saying that "extremist groups that set fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel's national security and foreign relations".
He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultra-nationalist ministers in Netanyahu's cabinet, had "brought the area to the brink of anarchy, and the authorities have yet to address the crisis".
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Netanyahu has not yet commented but Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks by a "handful of extremists" and said they are "against our values and do not represent the law-abiding citizens of Judea and Samaria" — the biblical names for the West Bank.
"Israeli authorities are firmly committed to enforcing the law against extremist violence," he told the ELNET Jerusalem Summit.
Israeli police open investigation
UN bodies and most countries of the world deny the legality of the settlements, which make the prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position Israel disputes.
Read more'We see our culture being stolen': How Israeli settlers are attacking West Bank olive groves
Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police had been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha'al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani "following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area".
Ben-Gvir replied in an X post that Eisenkot's condemnation amounted to selling out to Arab parties, which could become part of a possible new government. Smotrich favours settlement expansion and wants Israel to annex the West Bank.
Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, the largest Arab party in Israel's parliament, said the attacks were "the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has become an everyday occurrence", citing encouragement from Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.
Israel's parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government, after the election on October 27 stripped Netanyahu of his majority but left others with no clear path to power.
Read moreEisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot, who heads the centre-right Yashar, with forming a government, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.
Unless Eisenkot forms a unity government with Netanyahu, he is likely to need support from Arab parties to be able to count on a majority of parliament's 120 seats.
If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)

items.title: Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
items.summary:
Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
KC Current win NWSL championship as Spirit lose third consecutive final despite playing in front of rowdy home crowd.
Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears a
items.text:
Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
KC Current win NWSL championship as Spirit lose third consecutive final despite playing in front of rowdy home crowd.
Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.
For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.
This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.
The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.
The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.
And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.
“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.
After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.
“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.
“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”
That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.
Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.
The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”
For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.
The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.
The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.
Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.
“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.
“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”
KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.
Rodman scored from a header minutes later.
The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.
Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.
Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.
“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.
“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”
Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.
And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.
The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.
Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.
On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.
For the Spirit, Rodman was a young, rising star at the last tournament, but she heads into next year as one of the most renowned players in the sport as the USWNT push to reclaim the title from Spain.

items.text:
Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
- Published
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.
A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the pair kissing while surrounded by white roses.
Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, could be seen in the background of one image. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley.
Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said "I do" in a black suit from the same fashion house.
In one of the photographs, which was the first in a series of images shared by the singer in an Instagram post, the newly weds posed next to a golden retriever.
The post was captioned with "M+M" followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November.
Miley's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments.
The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra.
Guests stuck to an all-black dress code, according to reports.
- 'Angel by my side' - Miley Cyrus pays tribute to godmother Dolly Parton 
  - Published26 August
- Miley Cyrus confirms engagement to musician Maxx Morando 
  - Published3 December 2025
The American singer confirmed her engagement to the 28-year-old drummer during an interview with US TV show Good Morning America last year.
She said Morando had got down on one knee for the proposal during a trip to Asia.
"I am not easy to surprise because I love to control every situation and I had completely surrendered and I'm telling you, I was so, so, so surprised," she said.
During an interview with Wonderland, Morando said he "had to be really sneaky" to keep his proposal plans a secret.
"We went to Tokyo first for a couple days, and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could," he said.
Cyrus, 33, had previously been married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth but the couple separated in 2019.
The singer, whose hits include Party in the U.S.A and Wrecking Ball, married Hunger Games star Hemsworth in 2018 after the couple were in a relationship for a decade.
Speaking to British Vogue in 2023, Cyrus said she and 28-year-old Morando met after being "put on a blind date".
Morando is a drummer with LA-based band Liily. The band participated in NBC's Miley's New Year's Eve Party - hosted by Cyrus - in 2022, alongside musicians including Cyrus's late godmother Dolly Parton and David Byrne.

items.summary:
Chaotic week, nightmare start and huge reality check for Pochettino
- Published
"Sacked in the morning, you're getting sacked in the morning..."
Fourteen minutes in, arms folded, two goals down at Liverpool and with his Manchester United team reduced to 10 men, Mauricio Pochettino could not ignore t
items.text:
Chaotic week, nightmare start and huge reality check for Pochettino
- Published
"Sacked in the morning, you're getting sacked in the morning..."
Fourteen minutes in, arms folded, two goals down at Liverpool and with his Manchester United team reduced to 10 men, Mauricio Pochettino could not ignore the cruel taunts echoing around Anfield.
What on earth must Pochettino have been thinking as he stood at the edge of his technical area?
In distance terms, he was 3,800 miles from his last managerial assignment against Haiti in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.
In difficulty levels, it must have felt significantly further than that.
By the final whistle, as Liverpool's gleeful supporters alternated between singing about Pochettino's dismissal, United "going down" and celebrating "Poch is at the wheel", the Argentine head coach would have been starting to understand the scale of the task he has taken on by quitting his United States job in mid-season.
He had just watched United be dismantled 4-0 by their oldest rivals, with Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and two quickfire goals soon after representing just about the worst possible start imaginable to his reign as manager.
"Animals of the grass, we like to smell it and feel it," was the memorable phrase Pochettino came out with during Friday's pre-match media conference. Listen to former United skipper Roy Keane's post-match summary of the loss on Sky Sports and a very different smell comes to mind.
For the record, it was the joint-worst result for any new United boss, matching the 4-0 loss Lal Hilditch suffered against Bolton in October 1926.
Hilditch lasted 30 games and never managed another team.
Rubbish or fighting - how views differed on Man Utd performance
Keane is not one for holding back, so his response to his old side's latest setback was predictable.
"Fans are applauding the players [at the end]. Applauding what? Applauding rubbish," he said. "When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision-making?"
There were enough images of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox broadcast during the game by Sky Sports to suggest there is a wider debate to be had about the quality of the players at Pochettino's disposal.
On Friday, Berrada said this season's squad was "fundamentally better" than the one which finished third last season. Few would agree with that, and presumably Keane is among the group who would challenge Berrada's assertion.
Pochettino, 54, shed tears of emotion when he explained his difficulty in deciding to quit the United States job and take up an opportunity at a club he has flirted with for the best part of a decade but, only now, has been given the chance to coach.
It was easy to imagine him being reduced to tears again as Sunday's debacle unfolded, a nightmare afternoon in Liverpool coming at the end of a chaotic week of travel.
He arrived to begin his new role as United head coach on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.
The USA beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, with Pochettino flying directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game. He landed at about 11:30 GMT before heading to the club's Carrington training ground - and his feet have barely touched the floor since.
Pochettino was bullish when speaking to the media after this 4-0 defeat.
Although he began his first answer by saying he went to referee Sam Barrott after the final whistle to "present his respect", he became increasingly more forceful in his view Leny Yoro should not have been sent off.
After dismissing the sorry statistic that United have conceded 19 goals in their latest six games, because he didn't want to talk about results and performances that occurred before he replaced Michael Carrick, he then used Yoro's red card as the prism through which his side's entire performance at Anfield should be judged.
"What I learned from my players [today] is that they like to fight. They are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games," Pochettino said.
"Today we made an unbelievable effort. Today was a test. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action. Do you think that is easy?
"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more."
We were punished and they were not - Pochettino
It is a basic truth that Pochettino won six games this season as United States boss, twice as many as United have managed in 16 matches across all competitions. His new team have kept one clean sheet, against Azerbaijanis Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.
Pochettino's biggest selection call was to alter his defence by handing Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in almost 12 months.
It was a De Ligt misread of a bouncing ball that led to Yoro having to decide whether to foul Alexander Isak before he entered the penalty area.
"It was clearly a foul and he was clearly the last man," said home boss Andoni Iraola, giving his reading from a Liverpool perspective. "Will he score? We will never know."
Pochettino had a different opinion.
"If you go a minute and a half before, [Jeremy[ Jacquet and [Bryan] Mbeumo and compare it..." he said, suggesting his team should have been awarded an earlier penalty.
"Yes, it's painful because it's 4-0. But for us to play 80 minutes with 10 men is unfair. We need to be critical but the action of Liverpool [player] was also a mistake, no? But we were punished and they were not. That is the truth."
Pochettino takes his team, and his grievance, to Lisbon on Wednesday for a Champions League encounter with Sporting.
After that, it is Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry in the Premier League. This, to an extent, was a game United and their fans, and even Keane probably, expected little from.

items.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
items.summary:
A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.
Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our
items.text:
A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.
Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.”
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.”
But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement.
In Pachochki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.”
Pachochki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT 3.5.
“GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models,” he wrote. “Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.”
So in his view, perplexity could provide the basis for “a shared benchmark for general intelligence,” which AI companies could then use to establish “common limits.” With perplexity serving as a standard measurement for AI progress, the companies would commit not to go past a certain threshold “until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.”

items.text:
A beginner's guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
We have AI at home! Set up your own free personal ChatGPT on your PC with Unsloth and Inkling or Qwen. It's private, and the whole house can use it.
By Jerry James ·
With the launch of open-weight models like Qwen, cloud-based LLM providers seem like they're more of infrastructure or appliance businesses when it comes to most routine tasks that an AI model can handle.
OpenAI and Anthropic have displayed a pattern of dropping model quality in the 'latest' version and controlling exactly what you're allowed to run on their models. Add to this ballooning costs and privacy concerns, and we get a pretty good case for moving away from this 'convenient' cloud experience.
That's basically where I was too. I wanted to offload certain token-heavy research, data collection, or coding tasks to an AI model without staring at usage limits all day. So, as any reasonable human being would do, I decided to set up my own local AI: a Claude and ChatGPT replacement that runs at home on my own hardware.
Since this was my first attempt, my primary focus was keeping it simple and hosting it on Windows. If you're a beginner, you can follow along to get one going on your home network too.
Once you have the hardware sorted, it takes about 10-15 minutes (excluding download times).
The short version
Install Unsloth Desktop, download a quantized AI model that fits your GPU's VRAM, set your context size, and turn on LAN access so everyone at home can use it.
What Do You Need to Run a Local AI at Home?
Not much (other than the hardware). Here's a short list:
- A Windows PC with a graphics card (GPU). The more video memory (VRAM) it has, the bigger the model it can run. I'm using an RTX 5090 with 32GB VRAM for this setup.
- Unsloth Desktop. A free app that 'serves' the AI model to you through a chat interface. Get it from Unsloth.
- An AI model sized to fit your GPU. We'll pick one in the next section.
That's it. No terminal commands, Python environments, or subscriptions required.
Which AI Model Can Your GPU Run?
It depends on how much VRAM your graphics card has. As a rough guide, 8-12GB of VRAM handles smaller 9B-12B models, while 32GB comfortably runs 27B-35B models with plenty of room for long conversations.
On consumer-grade hardware, we'll need smaller models. The full-size Qwen model sits at around 56GB and won't really fit on a consumer graphics card unless you're running a Mac with unified memory. That's where quantization comes in.
What Is Quantization?
Quantization shrinks a model by compressing weights and moving to a lower precision. You basically trade some accuracy for a model that actually fits on your GPU and runs faster.
The same photo stored at 8, 4 and 2 bits per pixel. A model's weights lose detail the same way going from Q8 to Q4 to Q2.
If you're wondering whether this tradeoff is worth it, well, it depends. You'll find that certain types of workloads don't really care and give similar outputs, while others may be nearly unusable.
Which Model Should You Run for Your VRAM?
For this guide, we'll be going with Qwen3.8-27B with 4-bit quantization on my system with an RTX 5090. Going up a tier is an option thanks to its 32GB of VRAM, but I wanted to allow for a larger context window (how much of the conversation the model can keep in mind at once) rather than cramming in the largest model that fits.
Qwen3.8-27B at each precision with a 128K context, from our VRAM calculator. At 4-bit, the model and the context fit a 32 GB card with room to spare.
If you want to run a model of this caliber with excellent performance, a hilariously overpriced RTX 5090 (remember when $1,999 felt too high?) is unfortunately still not a terrible 'deal' these days. The other option is way more expensive enterprise-grade GPUs.
If you're on a GPU with less VRAM, you can still get something very usable going right away. The table below gives you a rough idea of where you can start.
Small
- 8-12 GB
- UD-Q4_K_S or Q4_K_M
- 8K-16K
Medium
- 16 GB
- Qwen3-14B, gpt-oss-20b (MoE), Gemma 4 26B (MoE), Qwen3-Coder-30B (MoE), Qwen3.6-35B (MoE), Inkling 2 Mini (MoE)
- Q4_K_M or Q5_K_M
- 16K-32K
Large
- 24 GB
- UD-Q4_K_M or Q4_K_S
- 16K-32K
Extra Large
- 32 GB+
- UD-Q4_K_XL or Q6_K
- 64K-128K+
Models marked MoE (mixture of experts) only run a few billion of their parameters for each token. They keep a decent speed on a smaller card with the rest held in system RAM, which is why a 35B model sits in the 16 GB row. On an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, our calculator puts Qwen3.6-35B at about 47 tokens per second this way.
Feel free to experiment with several models until you find one that fits your needs. You can also use GPUPartner's VRAM Calculator to get an estimate.
Can You Run Inkling 2 on an RTX 5090?
Inkling 2 Mini, yes. Inkling 2 Small, no.
Inkling 2 Mini is the newest model in this size class. Thinking Machines Lab released it on November 17, 2026: 26.4B parameters, Apache 2.0, vision support and a 1M-token context. Unsloth's recommended file, UD-Q4_K_XL, is 17.6 GB. That is within 0.1 GB of the Qwen3.8-27B file in this guide, so it sits on a 32GB card the same way and leaves about 14GB for context.
Nothing else in this guide changes. Update Unsloth Desktop first, because Inkling 2 needs a recent build, then search for Inkling 2 Mini in the same drop-down in Step 2.
2-bit
- 10-11 GB
- 12 GB card
3-bit
- 13-15 GB
- 16 GB card
4-bit (recommended)
- 17-18 GB
- 24 GB card
8-bit (lossless)
- 24 GB
- 32 GB card
Those figures are Unsloth's. They count RAM and VRAM together and cover the model alone, so a long context needs more. Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with 5.4B parameters active, so the 4-bit file also runs on a 16 GB card with the remainder in system RAM, a little slower.
Inkling 2 Small is small in name only. It is a 594B model, and the smallest file Unsloth publishes is 171.7 GB. That is unified-memory territory: a 256GB Mac Studio or a DGX Station, not a graphics ca

items.summary:
Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino.
This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferg
items.text:
Chaotic, bewildering, and on this evidence in a relegation dogfight: welcome to the three‑ring circus that is Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino.
This ended as a 4-0 rout in favour of Liverpool, the new head coach overseeing the poorest opening result of the eight who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Factor in this result coming against United’s fiercest rivals and Pochettino’s despair is complete.
He is firmly in the dock for this loss, due to a disastrous preference for Matthijs de Ligt over Harry Maguire, the hapless Dutch defender playing a leading part in three Liverpool goals.
Towards the end the Kop chirped: “You’re going down with the City.” There may be truth in the humour unless Pochettino gets hold – fast – of the rabble inherited from Michael Carrick.
Eight short minutes into a nascent tenure and a disgusted shake of his flowing locks was the greeting to the madhouse he has taken over. By then Leny Yoro had been sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak and Anfield was in bearpit mood.
Very far from ideal – and worse was to follow. Far worse. After the Frenchman departed, Dominik Szoboszlai smashed the free-kick through a nonexistent wall and beyond Senne Lammens and Liverpool were 1-0 up.
The visitors’ next act? To enter full meltdown as Diogo Dalot allowed Rio Ngumoha room to cross and Florian Wirtz hooked home, De Ligt losing his man.
Thirteen minutes in and 2–0 behind made Omar Berrada’s talk of the “buzz” of Pochettino’s entrance at United farcical and made the chief executive appear to be as much as a chump as his latest appointee, who was authoring a new head-coach plummet, not bounce.
Yoro had been forced into hauling down Isak after De Ligt lost first the ball, then the Liverpool striker. De Ligt’s inclusion was Pochettino’s headline selection move, the dropping of Maguire handing the centre-back a first league start in a year and it backfired almost immediately.
“I don’t know who played the last game – we assessed the squad from the day we arrived and we believe it’s the best team for today,” Pochettino said beforehand when quizzed about the XI he sent out.
Words to haunt him and, as De Ligt’s only other start was in United’s 4-1 humiliation at Como last month in the Champions League, questions regarding the coach’s judgment were already being posed.
By now “sacked in the morning” was the derisory cry of Kopites as Pochettino’s new project was in the damage-limitation mode of a 5-3-1 with 21 minutes played, as off went Bryan Mbeumo for Maguire.
After spells with Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA, Pochettino’s honours roll reads one Ligue 1 and one Coupe de France – a modest two trophies in a 17-year managerial career.
Losing a Champions League final (with Spurs) and two EFL Cup finals (Spurs and Chelsea) had characterised him, to some, as a “bridesmaid” and at half‑time his team were definitively second best, fortunate to be only two behind.
In the perpetual soap opera that is United, the buildup featured a drone filming Pochettino’s first training session, Berrada’s interview and Bruno Fernandes saying new contract talks between the captain and club were paused due to the worst league start in 40 years.
Going into the game, United’s dire form contained a solitary win in 10 league matches and eight points. Why? Because they are a rabble, lacking cohesion from goalkeeper to attack, with individuals consistently embarrassing themselves and the shirt.
It cost Carrick, culpable for this too, his job and cleared the path for Pochettino to occupy a role he has long coveted. Each new manager since Ferguson has faced a two-pronged challenge: the state of the squad and the state of the club – each related.
Those who know Pochettino say he will bring charm and warmth – useful, maybe, for man-managing a group of multimillionaires, but at the interval he needed to perform the miracle of convincing them that something, somehow, could be salvaged after a diabolical opening 45 minutes.
They were staring at defeat by an Andoni Iraola side that began 10 points and 15 places better off. Pochettino hoped to avoid this by taking off Matheus Cunha for Joshua Zirkzee for the second half but ended the non-contest ashen‑faced, with Berrada and Jason Wilcox, the director of football, appearing just as lost in the posh seats.
A main takeaway from Berrada’s interview was his conviction that “we are heading in the right direction”. When he spoke United were 18th, and by full time they were 19th, with De Ligt a glaring emblem of their disarray. When again he was marking air not Isak, the Swede saved the centre-back more blushes by spraying wide.
This had Pochettino applauding, unfathomably, when invective seemed an apt response.
Yet when Ngumoha made it 3-0 after 66 minutes there was no more faux touchline enthusiasm from a man who had promised to “create something from scratch”. As with all who have followed Ferguson, he had discovered that United’s shaky foundations make building anything sustainable a sisyphean task.
De Ligt’s loose pass led to Víctor Muñoz’s fourth, meaning the answer to whether Pochettino’s debut could have gone any worse was a resounding no.

LPGA Tour: Jeeno Thitikul wins CME Group Tour Championship again and overtakes Annika Sorenstam's career money record
Jeeno Thitikul claimed a two-shot victory over Aki Iwai, with Nelly Korda finishing in third spot; Thitikul becomes the first player to win three consecutive CME Group Tour Championship titles and passes Annika Sorenstam in the LPGA Tour career money list
Sunday 22 November 2026 20:41, UK
Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida.
Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.
She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the final 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

items.text:
Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
- Published
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.
The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.
The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.
Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.
Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.
She conceded on Sunday, saying in a statement: "After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I'm humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short."
Hubbard, meanwhile, wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".
He added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District."
Hubbard's win, which comes after he lost to Foxx in the 2024 midterms by nine percentage points, followed a number of Democratic victories in deeply Republican districts including South Carolina, Texas, Alaska and Iowa.
Hubbard, like many Democrats running in the midterms, focused on the rising cost of living in the US during the war with Iran - a top issue for voters.
President Donald Trump himself has suggested inflation caused by the war in Iran was probably to blame for the Republican losses, as well as Vice President JD Vance.
Hubbard has also said he will also prioritise working families and small businesses, supporting public education and expanding access to affordable healthcare, according to his website.
The remaining House races yet to be called are in Tennessee and Minnesota, while two elections in Louisiana will go to a runoff in December. In Tennessee's fourth district, Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than 300 votes, and in Minnesota's first district, Democrat Jake Johnson is winning by fewer than 500 votes.
Democrats may use their upcoming majority in the House and control of the Senate to investigate conflicts of interest and other actions by the president and those close to him, while the Senate also has the power to confirm or block the president's cabinet and judicial nominations. They will also be able to pass legislation through Congress easily, though Trump still has to give final sign off for it to become law.
However, even with control of both chambers of Congress, they will still have limits on their power as Trump can veto legislation.

items.title: Gary Neville on De Ligt selection and 'negligent' Man Utd
items.summary:
Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Gary Neville on Matthijs de Ligt selection and 'negligent' Red Devils
Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card; Red Devils have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season
items.text:
Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Gary Neville on Matthijs de Ligt selection and 'negligent' Red Devils
Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card; Red Devils have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season - the most by any side in Europe's major leagues
Sunday 22 November 2026 20:32, UK
Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their defence as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.
Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.
United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.
"It's negligent," said Sky Sports pundit Neville.
- Match report | As it happened | Teams | Stats

- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW 📺
"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."
Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.
Watching back the opener, when De Ligt misjudged a high ball, Neville said: "The minute that De Ligt makes that run in that channel, Yoro has to come across within 10 metres of him, and [Diogo] Dalot has to come across. This is so bad from Yoro and Dalot.
"De Lift makes a right mess of it. He can't believe it though, De Ligt. He's played centre-half before. He can't believe Yoro's not there. Then Yoro makes contact and it's clumsy.
"Honestly. You can't get worse that that.
"You've got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they're in fear.
"De Ligt and Martinez have dropped off, Dalot's not coming quickly enough.
"It's a mess because of the fact they've got no confidence and haven't got the ability to play out there at Anfield in a game against Liverpool."
Neville 'very surprised' by De Ligt call
Neville was baffled by Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt, who was similarly poor when returning from injury in last month's 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.
"We were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," added Neville.
"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes.
"Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.
"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt.
"Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.
"I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como, he was all over the place in Como.
"It's almost like you don't know what's happening. I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well.
"I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either."
'That back four will get you relegated'
United's total of eight points after 11 games is their lowest at this stage of a season since the 1972/73 campaign.
"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," added Neville.
"A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.
"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact.
"The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly."
He added: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and [Lisandro] Martinez.
"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.
"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.
"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact."

items.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
items.summary:
Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democr
items.text:
Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.
House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in an election sweep unseen since 1992 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities.
Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in President Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018.
The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Four other House races remain outstanding: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff.
Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority.
The milestone in the 435-member House sets up divided government, with the Senate also in Democratic hands and with a Republican president in the White House. Emboldened Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda to address high costs of living while also confronting Trump with a vast oversight agenda for the remainder of his second term in office.
The Democrats’ majority will be bigger than any the party has seen in elections since Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 (258) or the election of Barack Obama in 2008 (257), yet not quite the high-water mark of the Franklin D. Roosevelt-era, which saw House Democratic majorities swell past 300.
It presents opportunities and challenges ahead.
“Like, hell yeah, we should feel pressure,” said Democratic Rep. Jason Crow of Colorado, a former Army Ranger.
“There are people dying in this country and people losing their healthcare, losing their livelihoods, losing their farms, being terrorized from ICE," he said earlier this month at the Capitol, referring to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. "If you don't feel a sense of urgency and pressure in this job, and a desperation to deliver for folks, then you don't belong under this Capitol dome."
The numbers underscore the extraordinary scale of Democratic wins, which spanned from the strongest Republican states to the Midwest and East Coast, as voters, angry over high prices and the Iran war and concerned over corruption, made clear their discontent with Trump.
Read morePeltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
Taking control of both the House and the Senate come January, the Democrats will carry with them the backing of voters and the expectations to deliver. The Senate Democrats won a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their biggest advantage in over a decade.
The Democrats, as part of their 100-day agenda, are planning swift votes to reverse the Republicans’ Medicaid cuts and restore the Affordable Care Act tax credits the Republicans allowed to expire.
Democrats have vowed to marshal their subpoena powers and launch a flurry of investigations to exert the role of Congress as a check on presidential power. That includes plans to probe how Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is in line to become House speaker, has not ruled out trying to impeach Trump for a third time.
“This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen,” said progressive leader Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., at the Capitol.
She called the big numbers "a mandate for change.”
Rep. Tom Suozzi, a centrist Democrat from New York and an accountant by profession, said the House Democrats should focus 75% of their time on affordability issues and 25% on accountability.
“Everything should be tied back to the people — and how it’s affecting the people,” he said.
For example, he said, as the Democrats launch investigations into Trump's financial dealings, they should be connecting the dots: “How does that affect people’s pocketbooks?”
The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their planned probes into the administration, going as far as claiming that such investigations — a standard oversight function of Congress — may amount to “blatant criminality.”
After House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., struggled to keep the House functioning for the past two years with a narrow single-digit majority — meaning a few GOP lawmakers could derail the agenda — the Democrats will have a wide margin that provides the new leadership much more room to maneuver.
Jeffries, who is poised to make history as the first Black speaker of the House if his colleagues elect him to the job on Jan. 3, 2027, will be able to lose dozens of Democrats on any given vote and still have the 218 needed for passage, in the face of GOP opposition.
"We're not a monolith — people come to the caucus with different ideas — it's OK,” said Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., who is expected to lead the Congressional Black Caucus.
Republicans saw their number of House seats fall to one of the lowest tallies in decades. They're far from the end of the Obama administration, when the House Republicans won 247 seats in the 2014 election and the rise of Newt Gingrich when they won 230 seats in 1994.
Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, who was elected by his colleagues to be the Republican leader in the minority, vowed to fight their way back to power.
“Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families,” Jordan said.
The GOP's high-water marks include the 1920 election, with 301 seats for House Republicans.
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

items.text:
Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.
Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.
The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.
Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.
Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.
Was the referee right to send off Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro?
Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.
Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.
VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.
The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.
Was Pochettino right to bench Maguire for Man United?
The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.
For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.
Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.
The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.
The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.
United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.
Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.
A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.
By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.
Their last defeat at Anfield was a 7-0 victory for the home side – a repeat was certainly possible had Liverpool been more clinical.
Matters were so bad that the former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher commented on Sky Sports that he “felt sorry” for de Ligt prior to his eventual substitution in the second half.
The consensus was that Pochettino made the wrong call before the start.
What other Man United changes did Pochettino make at Liverpool?
Yoro and de Ligt have been peripheral figures in their time with the Old Trafford club, for varying reasons including injury, but they were not the only big calls made by Pochettino.
Another injury-plagued player, Patrick Dorgu, was also given a start – and in a formation which was not wholly clear. The popular Amad Diallo was forced to make do with a place on the bench alongside Maguire.
Dorgu, whose form has been indifferent at best, can operate as a wide defender or attacker. It appeared as though he was given some licence on the left to get forward, with United reverting to a back four, Lisandro Martinez covering on the flank in defence and Diogo Dalot holding back on the right.
Whether it was a back four or five to begin with – the latter explaining the absence of the more forward-minded Diallo – United were quickly forced to the latter with the sending-off and the sacrifice of Mbeumo at the other end of the pitch.
Not only was the decision to pick two less experienced centre-backs at Anfield a monumental – and ultimately costly – call, the move to switch to an unfamiliar feel across the backline was a painful lesson for Pochettino, who himself is more accustomed to a 4-2-3-1 setup.
What next for Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino?
With 19th-placed United mired in the Premier League drop zone, the UEFA Champions League appears a sideshow, but a trip to Sporting Lisbon awaits on Wednesday.
In some ways, Europe’s elite club

items.text:
Russian warship hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a suspected Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials. The strike severely damaged the warship and ignited a fire at the facility in what appeared to be the latest attack in Libya linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship Sunday at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.
They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
Read moreRussia turns to Libyan ports after Assad's ouster in Syria
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Sunday caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.
The vessel had docked at the base for refueling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.
A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. There was no immediate comment from either Russia or Ukraine.
On Sunday evening, local media said that another sea drone hit a commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack. No further details were given. The Almasar satellite television channel said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.
The western Libya government expressed concerns about “dragging Libyan ports and civilian facilities into external conflicts,” in an apparent reference to the war in Ukraine.
“The government reaffirms its categorical rejection of turning Libya into an arena for international conflicts or a theater for external powers to settle scores,” it said in a statement.
In March, Ukrainian forces operating in western Libya under a covert deal struck a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in a suspected sea drone attack near Maltese waters, Libyan officials said at the time.
The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, operated mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also at other military facilities in the capital, Tripoli, and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press.
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

The Listening Post
Cockroaches, dissent and a paradigm shift in India
The rise of Cockroach Janta Party and what it reveals about the future of politics and journalism in India.
A youth-led movement born as online satire has unsettled Indian politics. Named after a dismissive remark by the chief justice, the Cockroach Janta Party has mobilised some of the country’s biggest protests in years. They have been driven by anger over exam leaks, unemployment and a lack of political accountability.
The demonstrators have been met by heavy police crackdowns and clashed with mainstream media outlets they accuse of serving the government.
As young Indians turn to social media and independent outlets to tell their stories, this film examines the growing divide between India’s youth and mainstream media and what it could mean for the future of politics and journalism.
Contributors:
Manisha Pande – Editorial director, Newslaundry
Ashutosh Ranka – Co-convenor, Cockroach Janta Party
Rajat Sethi – Visiting fellow, India Foundation

On China, is Trump bucking the US national security establishment?
On China, US is torn between the fears of the national security establishment and the prospect of expanded trade.
For decades, China was considered the top threat to continued US global primacy, and President Donald Trump’s moves to expand trade with Beijing – even on advanced technology – are rattling Washington’s national security establishment. So when former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that the US should sell advanced chips to China to maintain dominance over the AI market, the traditional national security hawks baulked. US political scientist Matthew Kroenig tells host Steve Clemons that “the only one who seems to be unworried is President Trump”.
