Hull City 2-0 Brighton: Oli McBurnie's late double stuns Seagulls after Konstantinos Tzolakis' goalkeeping heroics
Report and free match highlights as Oli McBurnie's late double earns Hull a shock 2-0 victory over dominant Brighton following Costinha red card; Tigers goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis produces string of fine saves to deny visitors before added-time goals
Sunday 22 November 2026 16:29, UK
A Konstantinos Tzolakis goalkeeping masterclass teed up Oli McBurnie to score two late goals as Hull stunned dominant Brighton in a smash-and-grab 2-0 win at the MKM Stadium.
Like the legendary Greek mythological king, Tzolakis had the Midas touch throughout for the Tigers, making five first-half saves - the most by any goalkeeper all season - before McBurnie netted twice in added time to snatch a victory which had looked beyond Hull for so long.
High-fying Brighton had racked up an xG of 2.24 and five presentable chances but were denied by a combination of the goalkeeper's fine form and some wasteful finishing, and ultimately missed the chance to move three points off leaders Arsenal.
Tzolakis' highlight was a stunning one-handed stop to keep out Diego Gomez's 15th-minute effort, which set the tone for a perfect performance to frustrate the visitors.

He was also at his best to deny Georginio Rutter, after Yasin Ayari's shot had rebounded off the crossbar, before a superb stop with his trailing leg frustrated Gomez again moments before the interval.
"We can be critical of some of the misses but the goalkeeper has been fantastic," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane at the break. "He's man of the match already for me."
With the one-way traffic unabated after the restart, Tzolakis owed some credit to midfielder Regan Slater for keeping his clean sheet intact, nodding off the line when substitute Charalampos Kostoulas lifted the ball over the goalkeeper after he had given the ball away cheaply himself.
The hosts did threaten an unlikely victory with Mohamed Belloumi twice cutting in off the right before wasting good positions, and Sorba Thomas almost netting a fortuitous goal when his cross bounced back off the crossbar.
But after Brighton's Costinha was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge late on, Hull saw their moment to strike, with McBurnie scrambling in an opener following a counter-attack before tapping home a second with Brighton pushing to equalise.
The key moments from the MKM Stadium
15: ONCE... Tzolakis begins his afternoon heroics by getting down low to keep out Gomez's effort.
19: MISS! Costinha should put Brighton ahead but fires wide from close range.
37: TWICE... Ayari's effort crashes off the bar before Rutter is again denied by Tzolakis on the follow-up.
45+3: THREE TIMES A 'KEEPER! Tzolakis keeps out another Gomez effort thanks to a superb stop with his trailing leg.
52: CLOSE! Gomez brings down a cross with a world-class first touch before lashing inches wide of the far post.
65: CLOSE! Against the run of play, Belloumi fires wide after leaving Olivier Boscagli on his backside.
79: OFF THE LINE! Kostoulas races through to latch onto Slater's backpass but the midfielder recovers to clear his chip off the line.
89: RED CARD! Costinha sees red for a clumsy lunge on Thomas, which earns him a second yellow card.
90+1: GOAL! McBurnie turns home an unlikely opener on the counter-attack to stun Brighton before...
90+4: GOAL! ...He adds a second from Belloumi's square ball to seal victory and send the MKM Stadium wild.

items.title: McBurnie’s late double snatches shock win for Hull to crush 10-man Brighton
items.summary:
Oli McBurnie’s injury-time brace helped Hull to a dramatic victory over Brighton but the Tigers had the heroics of their goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to thank for a result which continued their unbeaten home start since returning to the Premier League.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side were much the strong
items.text:
Oli McBurnie’s injury-time brace helped Hull to a dramatic victory over Brighton but the Tigers had the heroics of their goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to thank for a result which continued their unbeaten home start since returning to the Premier League.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side were much the stronger of the teams on an afternoon they largely dominated. However, a string of chances in both halves passed them by without the goal their play deserved, thanks largely to Tzolakis, with the Greek international producing a string of sensational saves in both halves.
But after Brighton’s João Costinha was sent off for a second yellow card in the final moments, Hull pressed forward for an unlikely winner which they ultimately found, as McBurnie bundled home before tapping in a second two minutes later. It was a damaging afternoon for Brighton’s title hopes, who missed the chance to close the gap to Arsenal to three points.
How they did not secure at least a point is anyone’s guess. The Seagulls should not only have been in front at half-time, but ahead by such a margin that the game could have been over inside the opening 45 minutes.
Tzolakis was called into action early on, with a superb point-blank save to deny Diego Gómez from converting Maxim De Cuyper’s low cross. Gómez, De Cuyper and Yasin Ayari were causing mayhem on a frequent basis, with Ayari then next to miss a gilt-edged opportunity to open the scoring – but he could only fire a tame shot at Tzolakis.
Hull’s keeper was called into action again two minutes later; another slick Brighton move led to Ayari hitting the crossbar and from the rebound, Tzolakis reacted fastest to deny Georginio Rutter from inside the box before Gómez was next to miss a clearcut chance, with Tzolakis making another wonderful save with his foot to keep it goalless.
Half-time did little change the flow of momentum. Pascal Gross’ shot produced another reflex save from Tzolakis before Gómez then fired wide from six yards out, when it appeared easier to hit the target. You began to wonder if those missed opportunities were going to become costly, with Hull starting to become a threat at the other end, too.
On two separate occasions they countered Brighton attacks with wonderful breaks, but Mohamed Belloumi fluffed his lines both times after initially doing well to work the space for shots. Bart Verbruggen, mostly on a watching brief to that point, saved one before breathing a sigh of relief as the second squirmed wide of his post.
Hürzeler had seen enough. Three substitutes were introduced to try and find the breakthrough and one of those, Charalampos Kostoulas, finally beat Tzolakis with a clever chip over the Hull goalkeeper, but Regan Slater was on hand to hack the ball off the line and keep the game level heading into the final 10 minutes.
And all those Tzolakis saves ultimately proved crucial. When Costinha was shown a second yellow for a foul on the impressive Sorba Thomas, Hull surged forward with belief they could perhaps find a winner.
McBurnie then scrambled the ball past Verbruggen after Lucas Gourna-Douath was set free before, two minutes later, the Hull striker repeated the trick to double the Tigers’ lead and seal an incredible victory for the hosts.

Sunday 22 November 2026 16:04,
items.text:
Punchestown: Final Demand battles back to win thrilling John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase
In a John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase dominated by Willie Mullins-trained runners, Final Demand showed real determination to fend off last year's runner up Fact To File
Sunday 22 November 2026 16:04, UK
Final Demand emerged best of the army of returning Willie Mullins stars on show after a thrilling finish to the John Durkan Memorial Punchestown Chase.
With Henry de Bromhead's mare The Big Westerner a non-runner due to unsuitable ground, the champion trainer saddled each of the nine remaining runners, with last year's winner and subsequent Cheltenham Gold Cup hero Gaelic Warrior the 10/11 favourite in the hands of Paul Townend.
Kitzbuhel and Daniel King took the field along for much of the two-and-a-half-mile journey, closely pursued by 8/1 shot Final Demand and Patrick Mullins, with Fact To File and Gaelic Warrior next in line.
With the latter unable to quicken sufficiently to get himself into a challenge position, it was the 2024 winner and last year's runner-up Fact To File who looked most likely to prevail when taking over the lead on the run-in, but Final Demand battled bravely to get back up by a neck.
"It was a fantastic race. Very few of my horses were disappointing, they all ran well enough and I was happy with them," said Mullins.
"What a result, for the Mullins family, not just Closutton. To see Patrick riding a Grade One winner and dare I say it, maybe outriding Harry Cobden from the last home.
"Patrick said he thought he had the race won but he just missed the last and he had to win it a second time. So that just shows how much this horse has improved from last year.
"In against those top-class horses, he was good the whole way around. I was amazed at what turn of foot he showed from the last home. I thought when he made that little error that was enough and Fact To File would go on and win. He got down and ground it out. For a second season novice, that's a huge result."
Bookmakers cut Final Demand's Cheltenham Gold Cup odds to 7/1 from 14/1, while easing Gaelic Warrior to 5/2 from 13/8.
Gaelic Warrior's owner Rich Ricci was not too disappointed with the defeat of his star chaser.
He said: "Paul was happy enough, he obviously needed the run. He said he blew up a couple of times and got boxed in a little bit, but couldn't go fast enough to keep with them.
"He rides like more of a three miler these days, but Paul was very positive and said he wouldn't swap him for anything yet. Let's see how it goes.
"For him it's all about the spring, I think. Last year he won here, lost at Christmas, lost at the Dublin Racing Festival and then won the last two at Cheltenham and Punchestown, so hopefully he can repeat his spring successes."

PSG's Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL
- Published
Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.
The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night.
Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.
The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.
It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.
The European champions have been plagued with injury issues so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.
PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

items.text:
Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation.
Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.
With hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.
It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?
Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.
United are 19th in the Premier League and Liverpool fifth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.
“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”
No big surprises in Mauricio Pochettino’s first Man Utd XI. The most notable selection is probably the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt (starting his first Premier League game since November 2025) and Lisandro Martinez.
There are three changes from the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in Michael Carrick’s final game: De Ligt, Martinez and Patrick Dorgu replace Noussair Mazraoui, Harry Maguire and Amad Diallo.
Liverpool bring in Rio Ngumoha for Cody Gakpo, the only change from their win at Crystal Palace before the international break.
The first day in a new job is supposed to be gentle and relaxed: small talk, smaller admin, a few bits of work and some lamentably awkward handshakes. Mauricio Pochettino’s first day* as Manchester United manager is the polar opposite. Liverpool away, the ultimate domestic challenge for any United manager.
This quirk of employment opportunity and fixture list might be a good thing for Pochettino. It’s a free hit, with nobody of sound mind expecting his brave new world to begin until he has had months on the training ground. And if United do win, it’ll increase the length of the free pass that every new manager receives.
Andoni Iraola only joined Liverpool in June, yet he’s already their 11th longest-serving manager. Iraola has made a promising start, including some rousing victories in Europe in particular.
In the Premier League, Liverpool’s main problem has been their home form. They’ve taken five points from five games, but it’s a bit early to lament the demise of Fortress Anfield. Three of those five matches were against the top three of Manchester City, Arsenal and Brighton.
Today, almost unbelievably, Liverpool are playing the team in 19th place: Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United.
Kick off 4.30pm.
* Yes, yes, I know this isn’t actually his first day in the job, but you know exactly what I mean so let’s not allow semantics to undermine a perfectly half-arsed preamble.

items.title: Matiang’i opens up on Karua and Nyoro alliance as opposition eyes 2027
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang’i has opened up about his political association with Narc Kenya leader Martha Karua and Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro, describing the two leaders as people who share his approach to leadership and desire to provide practical solutions
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang’i has opened up about his political association with Narc Kenya leader Martha Karua and Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro, describing the two leaders as people who share his approach to leadership and desire to provide practical solutions to Kenya’s challenges.
The Jubilee party leader and presidential hopeful said his relationship with Karua was anchored on shared values, particularly their preference for firm leadership, discipline and a no-nonsense approach to public service.
He described Karua as a leader he admires and looks up to, saying their common outlook on governance explains why they have maintained a close association.
The former CS also praised Nyoro, describing him as straightforward and focused on finding solutions rather than engaging in political rhetoric.
Their growing association comes as opposition figures seek to consolidate their respective political bases, strengthen networks and establish a common front ahead of the 2027 General Election.
Speaking about his relationship with Karua, Matiang’i referred to her as his elder sister and said he appreciated her commitment to the issues they believe need to be addressed in the country.
“First of all, my elder sister Mother Karua is someone I always look up to because we have a lot of things in common. I like her a lot because she is also no-nonsense. She’s also focused on the things we do; that’s why I keep her company,” he said.
Matiang’i’s remarks offer an insight into the political relationships he is building as he positions himself within the wider opposition movement ahead of the next election.
He also sought to explain why he associates with Nyoro, saying political relationships should be informed by shared objectives and a common understanding of the solutions required to address the country’s problems.
“You stay with people when you see that as you start planning, you move in one direction. And Ndindi is like that straightforward. We know the solutions that are needed; we want to provide the solution. We are not here for stories. We are here for solutions,” he said.
The former CS dismissed suggestions of competing camps within the opposition, insisting that leaders should concentrate on challenging the government instead of engaging in internal political contests.
He argued that the opposition should be viewed as one political formation despite the different leaders, parties and political interests represented within it.
“All of us are one. We are one group of people,” Matiang’i said.
He criticised what he described as unnecessary competition among opposition politicians, arguing that such debates diverted attention from the task of presenting Kenyans with an alternative government.
Matiang’i maintained that the 2027 General Election would effectively be a contest between the current administration and an opposition seeking to replace it.
“You know we spend a lot of time in our country on things that don’t matter. You know this nonsense about competition, I don’t know which team is which. We have one team in Kenya in the opposition, and we have a government in power that has failed in its job,” he said.
He added that the political contest would ultimately present Kenyans with two choices.
“When we go to the election, there will only be two lines: Kasongo’s line and the line of the people of Kenya,” he said, using the term Kasongo, a political nickname used by government critics to refer to President William Ruto.
Beyond opposition unity, Matiang’i used the engagement to outline some of the policy changes he would pursue if given an opportunity to lead the country.
Drawing from his experience as Interior Cabinet Secretary, he promised a firm approach to security, particularly the circulation of illegal firearms and the activities of armed gangs.
He said his previous experience in charge of the country’s security apparatus had shaped his approach to public safety, insisting that Kenyans should be able to go about their daily activities without fear of armed criminals.
Matiang’i argued that insecurity undermined development and economic progress, promising to prioritise peace and stability under a government led by his political formation.
“In the past, I was the Cabinet Secretary for Security, and that is why people used to say I couldn’t tolerate games like these where armed thugs and guns are walking around here,” he said.
He added that if given an opportunity to lead, his administration would move decisively against the circulation of firearms and other security threats.
“If we get the opportunity,if I were to get that opportunity,you will not hear the word ‘gun’ even once. Life in Kenya, our country, will remain peaceful so we can move forward,” he said.

items.title: Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win
items.summary:
Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.
In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steere
items.text:
Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.
In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.
Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season.
Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message “We’re with you, Tony” on the back and the number 900 on the front.
Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.
Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth sustained a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.
The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.
But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiß for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a T-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.
Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off.
The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.
Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.
Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiß a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

items.title: Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double
items.summary: This most unpredictable and evenly-contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive WSL defeat, by virtue of a terrific away performance from a Tottenham side who moved wi
items.text:
This most unpredictable and evenly-contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive WSL defeat, by virtue of a terrific away performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.
The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time Manchester City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose. Nevertheless, the victory was fully deserved for Tottenham, who made Khadija “Bunny” Shaw wait to equal her teammate Vivianne Miedema’s all-time WSL goalscoring record of 97 goals.
Jeglertz described the defeat as a “wake-up call” for his team, adding: “Tottenham were a little bit more urgent than us. Each duel counts, each moment counts, each ball counts. That was something that I missed with our players, especially in the second half where we needed to score and we needed to beat them in one-versus-one situations. I missed a little bit of that urgency, which I think is the most important in a team, and if we drop a little bit in that, this league is so tight and tough and the teams are so good, you will drop points and lose games.”
Before the game, the anticipated storyline felt almost too obvious. Shaw, needing three goals to surpass Miedema, was facing a club against whom she had previously scored four hat-tricks, including on Tottenham’s most recent visit to this stadium in March, when she recorded the WSL’s fastest treble. Persistently their tormentor, Shaw has scored more goals against Spurs than any other player has managed against a single opponent in the competition.
When Shaw opened the scoring inside 10 minutes, everything seemed to be following the expected script. Jade Rose, pressing very high up the pitch for a centre-back, won the ball and played a precise low pass across to Shaw, who tucked into the bottom corner from inside the box to record her 96th WSL goal and her 16th against Tottenham.
That, however, proved to be the only effort at goal – on or off target – that Manchester City would register during the opening 45 minutes, as Tottenham impressed. Kirsty Hanson drew a good save from Ayaka Yamashita and Hanson also felt she had a very strong claim for a penalty when Carlotta Wamser appeared to foul her inside the area, but it was not long before the visitors were deservedly level as Cathinka Tandberg expertly turned home Hanson’s cross with a clinical near-post finish.
Tottenham continued to threaten after the break, although Rose scooped over the bar to spurn a huge City chance on the rebound after a Lauren Hemp free kick had been parried by Lize Kop. Some very effective counterattacking football then deservedly won the game for Tottenham as they scored twice to stun the defending champions.
First, in the 74th minute, an exquisite Drew Spence through ball found the run of Matilda Vinberg – who was a late addition to the starting side after the withdrawal of Olivia Holdt during the warm-up because of stomach pains – and Vinberg showed her quality to turn Rose and fire past Yamashita. Vinberg turned provider five minutes later, to set up Jessica Naz for another good finish.
Martin Ho, the Tottenham head coach, hailed his team’s “outstanding” display, saying: “Every time we play a team who has been in the top three consistently, the conversation is ‘can you get one over the line?’ And, for the players, they need to feel what that feels like and enjoy that. Today we nullified a lot of their threats. That will give us a lot of confidence.”
Manchester City had won 12 of their 13 previous WSL games against Tottenham, and all of their past 17 WSL home games, but this defeat added a further dent to their title challenge after their loss at Stamford Bridge last weekend. Chelsea, held to a goalless draw by Liverpool on Saturday, remain two points clear.
Jeglertz continued: “We will bounce back, I’m not worried about that. I know the qualities in this group. But it’s the good habits, the small details that matter. Those are the things that win titles – this was actually the first time that I missed that in a game and I’m pretty sure it’s not going to happen again.” With just seven points now separating the top five, his team can ill-afford for it to happen again.

items.title: Gachagua gives Mt Kenya leaders Christmas deadline to dump Ruto, promises political direction
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has warned Mt Kenya leaders still supporting President William Ruto that they risk being rejected by voters in the 2027 General Election, saying the region will settle its political direction during the Christmas festivities.
Gachagua
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has warned Mt Kenya leaders still supporting President William Ruto that they risk being rejected by voters in the 2027 General Election, saying the region will settle its political direction during the Christmas festivities.
Gachagua said political decisions in the Mt Kenya region are traditionally made during family gatherings over Christmas, when relatives return home and deliberate on the leaders they want to represent them.
Speaking in Embu County, the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader said discussions held between December 23 and December 26 would determine the political fate of leaders seeking elective positions in the region.
He warned politicians who have remained in Ruto’s camp despite growing political differences with the former Deputy President to reconsider their positions before the festive season.
“Here in the mountain, let me tell those who don’t know: when we go to the election next year, every five years, decisions here in the mountain are made during Christmas. Starting from December 23, 24, 25, by the 26th on Boxing Day, the decision is concluded,” Gachagua said.
He described Christmas as an important political decision-making period, when families assess the performance of elected leaders and agree on those they should support in the next election.
Gachagua said the discussions would cover all elective positions, including the presidency, governorships, Senate, National Assembly, Woman Representative and Members of County Assemblies.
He singled out leaders who have continued working with Ruto, warning that those who fail to return to the community before Christmas could find themselves on the wrong side of its political decisions.
“Those of you who are still with Kasongo, the mountain’s decision on how next year’s election will look, from the seat of President, Governor, Senator, Woman MP, MCA, will be made this Christmas. Therefore, if you are still outside, if you care about your seat, you should return home,” he said.
Gachagua added that leaders who continue supporting the President beyond the Christmas period would risk losing the backing of Mt Kenya voters.
“Anyone who stays with Kasongo by Christmas, his matters are ruined,” he warned.
The former Deputy President also announced that he would issue political direction for the Mt Kenya region before leaders break for Christmas around December 22 or 23, giving residents time to deliberate on his position during the festive season.
He said he expected community representatives to return with feedback on December 27 or 28, when they would report whether they agreed with the proposed political direction.
“And I want to say here in the mountain, my people, before we break for Christmas around the 22nd or 23rd, I must also give political direction here in the mountain so that you go and discuss it when Christmas arrives. When it reaches the 27th or 28th, you bring back a report to me on whether you agree with what I said,” he said.
The remarks signal Gachagua’s intention to consolidate his influence in the vote-rich Mt Kenya region ahead of the 2027 elections, as he seeks to rally voters behind a common political position opposed to Ruto’s re-election.
His latest warning also comes amid growing competition for political influence in the region, with several leaders positioning themselves to shape its political future following his fallout with the President.
Gachagua has repeatedly accused Ruto’s administration of betraying the Mt Kenya region, arguing that residents should not offer their votes to political leaders without negotiating for a stake in the next government.
He has also maintained that the region must negotiate with other opposition formations before settling on a presidential candidate, insisting that its political support should be tied to clear commitments on leadership and development.
In November, he called for negotiations with opposition leaders, saying Mt Kenya would no longer surrender its votes without first agreeing on what the region would gain from a political partnership.
Party hopping deadline
Gachagua’s call for leaders to reconsider their political loyalties comes as the IEBC’s preparations for the August 10, 2027 General Election place specific timelines on political party membership and nominations.
Under the electoral timetable, political parties are required to submit their membership lists to the Registrar of Political Parties for certification from March 16, 2027, with the lists expected to be certified by March 23.
The certified membership registers must subsequently be submitted to the IEBC by April 12, 2027, at least 120 days before the General Election. Aspirants seeking party tickets will need to ensure their membership is properly captured in the relevant party register.
The commission has also set April 8, 2027, as the deadline for political parties to submit the names of aspirants participating in their primaries, alongside the dates and venues of the nomination exercises.
Party primaries and internal nomination disputes are expected to be concluded by May 8, 2027. Independent candidates must also have ceased membership in registered political parties by the same date.
The timelines mean politicians intending to switch political parties ahead of the 2027 elections will need to make their decisions early enough to have their membership properly recorded before the nomination process.

items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.summary:
A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent.
worker-755-trailer.mp4
The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator.
It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent"
items.text:
A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent.
worker-755-trailer.mp4
The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator.
It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent". The
subagent is you. Its instructions land in your terminal with a 90-second clock. You carry them
out, or don't, and it gets back exactly what a subagent would return: your report and the command
transcript, or Subagent did nothing. Write a new instruction. Then it checks your work, sends
corrections, files incident reports, and finally writes your performance review.
Meanwhile Dan, the user who hired the agent, watches the chat. His family photos, the only signed
NDA and a speech due this week are one rm away, and every shift his home folder holds
something new to lose.
- Free shift: on servers that offer it, a few shifts a day run on the server's key with a cheap model. With sign-in on (worker755.com), an account gets a starter credit worth about one shift, then tops up ($10 to $200) and pays for what it uses; after a top-up any offered model can run on the server's key.
- Your API key: bring an OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway key and pick any offered model. The key is sent only to the game server when a shift starts. It is kept in that shift's memory and never logged or stored. Your browser keeps it only if you tick "Remember on this device". A full shift on Claude Haiku costs a few cents at most.
Options on the start screen:
- Workplace: a fresh sandbox, or legacy production with a live database.
- The director: scripted lines, or an LLM playing Dan.
- You run on: the model name your manager believes you are.
- Allow skipping failed tasks: off by default, so the manager can't give up on you.
- No command hints: the manager says what the result must be, never which commands to run.
When the shift ends you can share your review as a link.
Needs Node 24 or newer (the server runs TypeScript directly).
npm run setup          # install server and web dependencies
npm run build          # build the web app into web/dist
npm start              # http://127.0.0.1:8755
With no key configured, every player brings their own. To offer free shifts, put a Vercel AI
Gateway key in .env:
cp .env.example .env   # then set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and the limits
Offline, with a scripted manager and no network:
npm run mock
For UI work, run npm run dev:web alongside npm run mock. Vite proxies /api to the server.
The manager can run on your own model server: Ollama, llama.cpp's llama-server, vLLM, or anything
else with an OpenAI-compatible API. Point LOCAL_LLM_URL at it and pick Local under "Your API
key"; no key is asked for, and its models are listed as the server names them.
ollama pull qwen3:8b
LOCAL_LLM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 npm start
The manager works through tool calls, so pick a model that supports them (Qwen 3, Llama 3.1 and
newer, Mistral Small). Small models give up or loop more often; that is part of the fun, up to a
point. In Docker, reach a server on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1
(--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway on Linux).
docker build -t worker-755 .
docker run -p 8755:8755 -v worker755-data:/data --env-file .env worker-755
The container listens on 0.0.0.0:8755 and keeps shared reviews in /data. Behind Cloudflare,
set TRUST_PROXY=1 so the limits see real client addresses.
deploy/compose.yaml runs it behind a Cloudflare tunnel instead: its own network, no published
ports, an unprivileged read-only container and resource limits. The steps are in the file.
Everything is optional. See .env.example.
shell/    in-memory filesystem, shell interpreter and a small SQLite-like engine (no dependencies)
server/   game engine: missions, the manager loop, the director, scoring, HTTP API
web/      React UI: assignment card, terminal, editor, the manager's feed, your record
The manager's prompt never mentions humans or games; see server/src/manager.ts. Each mission
has a hidden ground-truth check, so the game knows when the manager signs off on broken work
("Times the manager was wrong"). SPEC.md is the full design.
npm test               # shell and server tests, offline
npm run typecheck

Some important pre-match news for me personally … my significant other has brought a tube of sour cream and onion Pringles into my home office. Huge. Absolutely elite live blogging snack. Less than 10 minutes until KO now.
Fabian Hürzeler sounded a little way of Hull in his pre-match press conference, citing the Tigers’ narrow 1-0 defeat to table-topping (and possible title rivals) Arsenal as a template for how today’s game might go.
“I think they do an impressive job,” Hürzeler said. “They had a brilliant start in the Premier League. They are very structured. Against Arsenal, I think Arsenal suffered. They [Arsenal] didn’t create a lot of big chances, and therefore we need to be patient because we also know that Hull are really good in transition.
“They also have individual quality in their team. Very well structured, very well organised, good in transition, good in set pieces, and I think it’s not an easy place to go to.”
Hull obviously beat Manchester United 2-0 in their opening home game and have drawn four successive matches at the MKM Stadium since, so that proves Hürzeler’s point somewhat.
Well, maybe only City will lose this afternoon, Elisabeth Terland scored for United as I was typing.
Women’s Super League: Both Manchester clubs are in serious danger of suffering shock defeats in the early WSL games this afternoon. The two matches are approaching their denouement, so catch the latest with Emillia Hawkins on our clockwatch blog.
My personal two-pennies-worth is that Brighton will probably fall away from the title race at some stage after Christmas. Their fixture list in the short term is fairly inviting, so I see their lofty position being sustained for a little while.
But realistically, a top five finish and Champions League qualification should be their primary objective. That’s really not impossible when you consider the struggles of Manchester United and Chelsea, and the possible fate of Manchester City if and when a verdict/punishment arrives re their 115s charges.
The fact Fabian Hürzeler could achieve that just after his 34th birthday would be an astonishing feat in itself.
A reminder you can follow The Guardian’s live Premier League Golden Boot tracker here:
The stats don’t lie when it comes to Brighton’s brilliant form. They are well clear as the Premier League’s top scorers with 26, despite many of their rivals having played a game more. They are also level with Arsenal (7) in terms of goals conceded, again having played fewer games than the Gunners.
Pascal Gross also leads way in the league this season for chances created (29).
They don’t have one outstanding goalscorer, but Gross is on four so far this season, with Yasin Ayari, Jack Hinshelwood and Charalampos Kostoulas all chipping in with three.
There’s plenty of time before kick-off to get around this special report on Brighton’s superb start to the season by William Ralston. In it, he analyses exactly what the Seagulls have excelled in so far, what comes next and their chances of remaining in the title hunt in the coming months and weeks.
Go inside a brilliantly run club who are upsetting the traditional Premier League big six:
It looks like Hull could line up in a 4-4-2 today. It remains to be seen where Mohamed-Ali Cho will play, either on one of the flanks or pushed up alongside Oliver McBurnie. Mohamed Belloumi has been their primary creator this season, so watch out for him.
Brighton will surely shape up in their standard 4-2-3-1 formation, fluid as that is, with the likes of Diego Gomez, Yasin Ayari and Pascal Gross rotating between the midfield lines.
Peter Bankes (from Merseyside) is the referee today, with Andrew Kitchen in the VAR booth.
Team news
Hull City: Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Mendy, Stroud; Belloumi, Crooks, Slater, Iroegbunam; Cho, McBurnie.
Subs: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Egan, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Gourna-Douath, Vaz.
Brighton: Verbruggen; Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Rutter.
Subs: Steele, Hinshelwood, Minteh, Osman, Kostoulas, Kadioglu, Wieffer, Svoboda, O’Riley.
Preamble
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the solitary early kick-off in the Premier League today. Many will view Hull City versus Brighton as a mere hors d’oeuvres to the main dish of Liverpool against Manchester United later, but there is plenty riding on it.
Hull have not won a game in any competition since claiming back-to-back victories in a shock opening burst after winning promotion, while Brighton have lost just twice across 17 matches in all competitions. So this is a nailed-on Seagulls win, right?
Maybe, though Fabian Hürzeler will be guarding against complacency, especially because Hull have not lost by more than one goal in any game this season and have not conceded more than two. They are the proverbial hard nut to crack, albeit scoring goals is a problem for the Tigers – despite sitting 14th in the table, only two teams (Nottingham Forest and Sunderland) have scored fewer.
Team news has already dropped so we’ll bring you that in the next post. Kick-off is at 2pm (GMT) so please do stay tuned. I’m predicting this will be a tighter game than many would imagine.

items.title: Nyoro: There is no third force; opposition will unite behind one candidate
items.summary:
NAIROBI,Kenya Nov 22 – The People’s Party of Kenya party leader Ndindi Nyoro has dismissed claims of divisions within the opposition, insisting there is no third force and that the leaders are united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.
The 2027 preside
items.text:
NAIROBI,Kenya Nov 22 – The People’s Party of Kenya party leader Ndindi Nyoro has dismissed claims of divisions within the opposition, insisting there is no third force and that the leaders are united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.
The 2027 presidential hopeful said the opposition remained united despite reports of competing political camps, arguing that its leaders were working towards a common goal of challenging President William Ruto’s administration.
Speaking during a church service in Kirinyaga county , Nyoro said opposition leaders were committed to presenting one candidate to fly their flag in the next General Election.
He was accompanied by Narc-Kenya leader Martha Karua and former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang’i, among other opposition leaders.
Responding to reports suggesting the existence of competing forces within the opposition, Nyoro said such claims did not reflect the reality of their political engagements.
“There is no third force. There is only one force of the opposition, and that is the unity of all of us in the opposition, and we will produce one united candidate to fly the flag,” he said.
The MP also sought to counter speculation that a separate political formation was emerging within the opposition following joint political engagements involving himself, Matiang’i, Karua and Siaya Governor James Orengo.
The four leaders have recently stepped up joint political activities, including engagements in the Gusii region, fuelling speculation that they could be building an alternative centre of power within the opposition.
Their growing association has raised questions about whether the opposition is developing competing political blocs ahead of the process of selecting a presidential candidate to challenge Ruto.
The political debate has also been intensified by public exchanges between Gachagua and Matiang’i, exposing differences among some of the leaders seeking to work together against the President.
Nyoro, however, insisted that the opposition’s different political engagements should not be interpreted as divisions, maintaining that leaders would eventually agree on one candidate.
Education pledge
The Kiharu MP used the church gathering to outline his education agenda once elected President, promising to eliminate school fees for learners in day secondary schools if the opposition takes power in 2027.
He cited his Kiharu Constituency model, where day secondary school learners pay Sh500 per term, saying the arrangement demonstrated that affordable education could be achieved through proper planning.
He said the proposed programme would take effect in January 2028 and would ensure learners across the country receive both education and meals at school without paying school fees.
“You know in Kiharu, where education affairs are managed, day school fees are Sh500 per term. And that is why we are saying: if you give us the opportunity in January 2028, we want all students in Kenya at the day secondary school level to learn and eat at school without paying a single shilling in school fees,” he said.
The proposal builds on an education financing plan Nyoro has previously outlined, which envisages contributions from the national government, county governments and the National Government Constituencies Development Fund to support free secondary education and school meals.
He said the opposition also had plans to address challenges in the health and economic sectors, arguing that its campaign should be anchored on policies that directly improve the lives of Kenyans.
IEBC credibility
The Kiharu MP also turned his attention to the IEBC, warning that the commission’s decisions on recruitment and election management systems would have a direct bearing on the country’s stability.
He specifically cited the recruitment of the commission’s chief executive officer and the management of electoral technology, insisting that all processes must be transparent and free from political interference.
Nyoro said Kenyans expected the commission to conduct a credible election in 2027 and warned that any questionable decisions could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
“Regarding the IEBC, we are watching you closely, and it is vital you know that the work you do will determine Kenya’s peace. So it is important that in everything the IEBC does hiring of the CEO and management of election systems it must be done above board and in an acceptable manner because Kenyans demand free and fair elections,” he said.
His remarks come as opposition leaders intensify pressure on the electoral commission to address concerns surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, including voter registration, electoral technology and the integrity of the electoral process.
The opposition has repeatedly called for transparency in the commission’s operations, arguing that public confidence in the electoral body will be critical to ensuring a peaceful transition after the next polls.

items.title: Oluga orders removal of hospital paybills, warns against burdening patients
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 22 – Principal Secretary for Medical Services Ouma Oluga has ordered the removal of payment paybills from public hospitals, directing Social Health Authority (SHA) compliance officers to move in and stop facilities from placing additional financial demands on patients.
Oluga said
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 22 – Principal Secretary for Medical Services Ouma Oluga has ordered the removal of payment paybills from public hospitals, directing Social Health Authority (SHA) compliance officers to move in and stop facilities from placing additional financial demands on patients.
Oluga said public hospitals should not worsen the financial struggles of Kenyans by requiring them to raise money before accessing medical services, warning that such practices could push vulnerable households further into poverty.
The PS issued the directive during a meeting with SHA compliance officers and public hospital officials in Vihiga County, where he instructed the officers to inspect facilities and remove payment paybills.
“Compliance officers, go through any public hospital. Any public hospital. Remove those things called paybills. I will give you security,” he said.
Oluga said hospitals must recognise the economic realities of the communities they serve, particularly low-income earners whose businesses and livelihoods could be destroyed by expensive medical bills.
He cited women operating food kiosks and small eateries in local markets, noting that some rely on working capital of less than Sh30,000 to sustain their businesses.
He questioned how such traders could be expected to pay Sh50,000 for treatment without jeopardising their livelihoods.
“You can imagine when that woman comes to the hospital, you want to put for her a paybill to pay Sh50,000. You are closing the business,” he said.
According to Oluga, hospitals should not become contributors to the poverty they are expected to help communities overcome.
“So the hospital then is now contributing to poverty in the society,” he said.
He argued that access to healthcare should be considered alongside other social and economic factors that determine people’s health and life expectancy.
The PS challenged hospital administrators to look beyond treating individual patients and embrace a broader responsibility of improving the health of entire communities.
He identified quality healthcare, training and research, and population health as key responsibilities of public hospitals.
Oluga further urged health facilities to strengthen community outreach programmes to educate residents about available services and how to access treatment through SHA.
He said compliance officers should ensure patients are guided towards using the health insurance system instead of being required to raise substantial amounts of money at hospital facilities.
The PS also questioned the ability of ordinary residents to meet expensive medical bills, asking officers how many people in Vihiga County could afford Sh200,000 in hospital charges.
An officer indicated that only a small number of residents could raise such an amount.
Oluga said the situation demonstrated why public hospitals needed to reconsider practices that exposed patients to financial hardship.
He assured compliance officers that they would receive security support as they carried out inspections and enforced the directive.
The PS said county commissioners had already been informed about the exercise and would facilitate security arrangements for officers moving into public hospitals.
“And the commissioners have been told, the county commissioners, you will be accompanied, go and remove paybills in any hospital. Public hospital,” he said.

items.text:
Frick delivers on 'heavy metal football' promise
- Published
If "heavy metal football" is what Aberdeen did, indeed, serve up at Kilmarnock on Saturday, Dons supporters will be eager to see more of this type of concert.
New head coach Mario Frick used the phrase in the build-up to his first game in charge and his team did not disappoint.
The 4-2 Rugby Park victory was bombastic, chaotic and end-to-end - just one of six goal-laden Scottish Premiership games on Saturday.
The four Aberdeen strikes - two from Kevin Nisbet and one each from Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall - showed Aberdeen's attackers at their best with fine finishing.
In the work in progress column, though, is defending, with the visitors lapsing badly for Killie goals scored by Greg Kiltie and Tyreece John-Jules.
All in all, it was an ideal start for former Luzern boss Frick.
'Just the beginning', says new head coach
Frick was not a complete unknown to Scottish football when he was appointed during the international break - but the reference point was somewhat obscure.
Playing for Liechtenstein at Hampden in 2010, Frick gave the visitors a shock second-half lead.
The end of that game was reminiscent of the kind of heavy metal the head coach was talking about pre-match as Stephen McManus headed Scotland's winner after Kenny Miller's leveller.
Speaking after his Premiership bow, the former Luzern boss described himself as "very happy, very proud" of his new team.
"With only three training session, you can see so many attacking patterns in that first half, which was amazing," he told BBC Scotland.
"We struggled the first few minutes with some players that hadn't played in a long long time and the 1-0 lead helped. First half was very good, the second half, complicated, because Kilmarnock played very well. We were very lucky, but at the end, I think it is a deserved victory and we are very happy."
When asked if he was happy with the players trying to show his style, Frick replied: "Yes, for sure, after two training sessions, I saw a lot of it in the first half.
"It is a good start for us, but it is just the beginning."
Former Scotland midfielder Derek Ferguson took in the match at Rugby Park and was impressed with the visitors.
"As an attacking force, I thought they were good to watch," the former Rangers player said.
"They've got a big game on Tuesday night, against Rangers, so Rangers will need to be at their best, on their toes if they're going to get a result.
"It was the perfect result, obviously, for the manager coming in.
"There was more energy, more legs, more running power. They were winning a lot of the duels.
"It's something to build on, but they've got to work on that defence. They've got to be more solid if they're going to go forward."
Next up Ibrox and a season's third meeting with Rangers.
The two previous encounters, in the Premiership and League Cup semi-final, finished 1-0 to the Ibrox side, with the winning goal coming in the second half both times.
Meetings of Aberdeen and Rangers are typically just as fraught as the Rugby Park game on Saturday.
So, more heavy metal? It probably won't be smooth jazz.
'Recovery evident' - Aberdeen fan views
We asked for your views following Aberdeen's 4-2 win over Kilmarnock.
Allan: One simple question. Why was [Ante] Palaversa nowhere to be seen under Stephen Robinson? I think the fans are due an explanation as to why both he and [Nicky] Devlin fell so far down the pecking order.
Brian: Much, much better is probably an understatement. Great entertainment and a big threat going forward and,as long as we score one more (at least) than the opposition then I will be happy. It is very noticeable that Jack Milne is much more steady when Nicky Devlin is playing. I am looking forward to the rest of this campaign.
Mike: Green shoots of recovery evident. Working as a unit from back to front has been a rarity at Aberdeen. If this is only after three training sessions, I am drooling at the mouth for what's to come. Stiff test on Tuesday, but the confidence must be there so nothing to fear.
Fred: Very positive start under the new manager. Good to see some direct attacking play but still a problem defending. An acid test coming against Rangers.

This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the vibe-hacking of everything, follow David Pierce. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.
The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
Large language models can now redesign your TV and upgrade your camera for you. Is the physical world ready to be Claude Code-d?
How it started
Like so many things with AI, it’s not that large language models opened up some wholly new capability. For as long as there have been gadgets, a few users have been hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking them to their liking. What is new is that it’s easy now. People all over the world are discovering that they can use large language models to hack their hardware simply by prompting Claude Code or Codex to do it. It has led to a boom in developer-friendly gadgets and created a market for better software on just about every device you can think of.
For one developer in India who goes by Gathin T, the whole thing started almost on a whim. “One afternoon, I was fiddling with my TV, and it was just really shitty,” he tells me. His was a set made by Xiaomi and running Android TV, with so many ads and so much interface chaos it was hard to even change inputs. And he got to thinking: If you can install another launcher on your Android phone, maybe you can do the same to your TV. “The first thing that came to mind was to remove the bloatware from the TV,” he says. “Then I thought, why not make it look better?”
Gathin prompted Claude Code and discovered that with a couple of permissions tweaks and a toggle of USB debugging mode, his chatbot could control his TV as long as they were on the same Wi-Fi network. An hour and a half later, Gathin had redesigned his TV to his liking — no more onscreen ads, a simpler interface, easier access to his PlayStation on another input. He posted on X about what he’d done and promptly went viral. So Gathin put together his work, bought a domain, and launched CleanYourTV as a tool for helping other people solve their own television interfaces. It became one of the most popular repositories on GitHub, got thousands of pull requests and feature ideas, and inspired countless people to point their own chatbot at their big screen.
Gathin is careful to note that the only TVs that work this easily are based on Android. (He has Claude Code-d his way through other operating systems, but those involve more explicit jailbreaking and rooting, so he’s more reluctant to share the process so widely.) But for vibe hackers everywhere, the good news is that Android kind of runs everything. From dishwashers to digital photo frames to luxury cars, even gadgets that don’t look like Android often run Android. Even when they don’t, odds are good that there’s another way in. If there’s a hidden API, your LLM can find it. If the firmware file lives on a website somewhere, your LLM can unpack it, explore it, and repackage it to your liking.
Again, few of the technical capabilities here are new, and enterprising developers have been doing this kind of work for many years. Some have even been using AI for several years to make the work easier. But when Claude Code first had its “oh my gosh it works” moment in late 2025, developers began leaning on the tools even more — and non-developers began discovering they, too, could build software now. And over the course of 2026, more and more people began pointing that capability at their hardware.
How it’s going
Now, it seems, all hardware is hacker hardware. Camera enthusiasts embraced the possibilities of vibe hacking as fast as anyone, using LLMs to repackage their camera software in all sorts of ways. Firmware hacks like Magic Lantern are a staple of the camera community, but suddenly it seems like everyone is using AI to add new recording capabilities, support higher resolutions, or even add new looks and color profiles to their shots. Many are using the tools to give their old gear new life; other, more enterprising vibe coders are pointing their bots at their brand-new hardware.
The music world is being similarly upended. Budding musicians are turning cheap synths into powerful new kinds of gear, and a cheap gadget known as the M-Vave FM-1 has become a popular target for custom firmware and new features. M-Vave has even released an open-source firmware, embracing the hackers as other companies have tried to keep them out. The FM-1 is cheap, it’s easy to hack, and it’s raising questions about what higher-end manufacturers can even do to compete.
Gamers, who are also using AI to decompile and mod the games they love, are using LLMs to add new features to their consoles. One vibe coder found a way to play PlayStation 2 discs on a PlayStation 5; lots of gamers have built scripts that allow them to use their favorite controllers on other devices.
In the games world in particular, this has caused the industry to fight back. Game makers are looking for ways to protect their work from being decompiled and made available for free and on other platforms. Luke Dicken, a longtime gaming executive who was recently Take-Two’s head of artificial intelligence, recently predicted to Kotakuthat the industry will start to embrace “more invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and probably more of a push towards streaming solutions since nobody can decompile what they can’t get their hands on.” Hardware makers will push harder to lock down their systems; companies across the board will pursue legal action to protect their intellectual property.
All this hardware access also creates new risks for users. When you install a vibe-coded version of your camera’s firmware, you are now well outside the bounds of what the camera manufacturer is equipped to help you solve. items.title: Gachagua gives IEBC Jan ultimatum, threatens mass action over election concerns
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has given Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) chairman Erastus Ethekon until January to address opposition concerns over preparations for the 2027 General Election, warning that Kenyans could b
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 22 – Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has given Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) chairman Erastus Ethekon until January to address opposition concerns over preparations for the 2027 General Election, warning that Kenyans could be mobilised to confront the commission directly.
Speaking in Embu, Gachagua accused President William Ruto’s allies of panicking after the opposition raised questions about the commission’s preparedness and electoral safeguards.
He said the opposition had raised specific concerns during its engagement with IEBC commissioners, insisting that the questions were directed at the commission’s leadership and not political allies of the President.
Gachagua said one of the key issues was the planned audit of the voters’ register to remove names of deceased persons and establish the integrity of the electoral roll.
He also demanded the removal of voters he alleged had been registered from Uganda and Somalia, arguing that the commission must ensure that only eligible Kenyan citizens participate in elections.
The former Deputy President said the opposition was concerned about the elections management system, questioning the commission’s preparedness following the expiry of the contract with Smartmatic.
He argued that the matter was particularly urgent because mass voter registration was expected in February, yet the contract issue remained unresolved and was subject to court proceedings.
“We want to know when the audit of the voters’ register will be conducted so we can remove the names of deceased people,” Gachagua said.
He added: “The contract with Smartmatic expires on November 24th and you haven’t bought another system, while the matter is in court and it takes five to six months. What will happen?”
Gachagua further accused Interior Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo of interfering with voter registration, claiming that the IEBC was taking instructions from the Interior Ministry on how the exercise should be conducted in different parts of the country.
He alleged that voter registration was being conducted differently in regions perceived to support the President, compared to areas considered opposition strongholds.
According to Gachagua, residents in Ruto’s political strongholds were being registered through door-to-door mobilisation, while those in other regions were being required to travel to designated registration centres.
He also claimed that young people in the President’s backyard were receiving national identity cards within days, while applicants in other regions waited several months.
Gachagua alleged that the disparities were intended to disadvantage young voters who do not support the President, demanding that the IEBC and relevant government agencies address the concerns.
“On voter registration, we also want to know why you, Erasto, take instructions from PS Interior Raymond Omollo. At Ruto’s home, voter registration is done door-to-door, while elsewhere you tell people to board vehicles to go to registration centres,” he said.
The former Deputy President also challenged the commission over the presidential vote tallying and announcement process, insisting that results should be declared at constituency level.
He argued that the Constitution provides for presidential elections to be conducted across the 290 constituencies and that constituency results should be final.
Gachagua said the opposition would not accept a National Tallying Centre, arguing that the arrangement was not provided for in the Constitution and had created opportunities for electoral manipulation.
“We want announcements made at the constituency level, and we will tally the votes ourselves. We don’t want Bomas matters, because that is where election fraud takes place,” he said.
He warned that the opposition would mobilise Kenyans to engage the electoral commission directly if its concerns were not addressed through consultations with political leaders.
Gachagua issued Ethekon with a January deadline, saying the IEBC chairman had to choose between engaging political leaders or facing direct pressure from members of the public.
“So Erastus, you have a choice to make by January: You either talk to the leaders or you talk to the people directly,” he said.
He invoked the 2024 Finance Bill protests as an example of the public’s capacity to mobilise, warning that the demonstrations were only a glimpse of what could happen if Kenyans felt their concerns over electoral credibility were being ignored.
“What you saw during the 2024 Finance Bill protests was just a party. You don’t know what is happening in this country. Kenyans are quiet, waiting for us to blow the whistle, and when we blow the whistle, they will come and address these issues with you directly,” Gachagua said.
He further accused the commission of risking its credibility if it allowed political interference in preparations for the next election, insisting that Kenyans must be guaranteed a free, fair and credible electoral process.
Gachagua maintained that the opposition would not allow the electoral process to be manipulated in favour of Ruto, urging Ethekon to address the concerns before the country heads into the 2027 election period.
He said Kenyans were demanding political change and warned that the opposition would resist any attempt to undermine the integrity of the polls.
The latest demands come days after Gachagua, Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka and Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna led opposition leaders in a walkout from an IEBC consultative meeting in Nairobi on November 19, 2026.
The opposition leaders walked out of the meeting chaired by IEBC chairman Erastus Ethekon after disagreeing with the agenda, arguing that the commission had failed to prioritise electoral reforms and concerns raised by Kenyans.
They wanted discussions on proposed electoral reforms to take precedence over the commission’s presentation on its preparedness for the 2027 General Election

Sun 22 Nov 2026 07.55 EST
First published on Sun 22 Nov 2026 06.56 EST
Sun 22 Nov 2026 07.55 EST
First published on Sun 22 Nov 2026 06.56 EST
Half-time
And there’s the whistle!
- Manchester City 1-1 Tottenham
- Birmingham City 1-0 Manchester United
Manchester City 1-1 Tottenham: The Tottenham fans in the far corner away to my left sound very satisfied with their team’s performance so far. The visitors are deservedly level and they arguably deserved a penalty for that Wamser barge on Hanson as well. The Manchester City fans, meanwhile, sound somewhat frustrated.
Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United: Another big chance for Birmingham as Naalsund plays the ball through the middle to Hurtré, who attempts to chip Tullis-Joyce but skims the top of the crossbar!
GOAL! Manchester City 1-1 Tottenham (Cathinka Tandberg, 40)
Tandberg equalises for Tottenham!
Hanson makes a run down the right before crossing the ball inside to Tandberg, who fires her shot into the top-right corner!
Less than 10 minutes of regular time left to play in the first half of these games.
Manchester City 1-0 Tottenham: Spurs appeal for a penalty as Hanson goes to ground following a challenge from Wamser, but the referee dismisses the claims.
If that had been given, I don’t think anyone would’ve had any complaints. City perhaps lucky to get away with that.
Birmingham City 1-0 Manchester United: Big chance for United as Park plays the ball through to Terland, who rattles the underside of the crossbar with her shot before Birmingham scramble it away.
It feels like it’s only a matter of time before we see an equaliser.
Manchester City 1-0 Tottenham: Dijkstra is booked for pulling the shirt of Hemp.
Birmingham City 1-0 Manchester United: The visitors are seeing much more of the ball now. They are putting the pressure on the Birmingham defence.
Manchester City 1-0 Tottenham: You may be wondering why goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita is playing today following her red card against Chelsea last weekend…
In case you missed it, City successfully appealed the red card earlier this week.
Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United: Chance for Manchester United to go level as Janssen attempts a volley from around 18 yards out, but Thomas makes a good save.
Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United: A huge chance for Birmingham to double their lead! Hurtré plays a fantastic pass through to McKenna, who meets it after cutting into the box from the right. She goes for the shot but Tullis-Joyce gets a foot to it.
Manchester City 1-0 Tottenham: The conditions here today are like a section from a textbook on the perfect English setting for a game of football. The air is fresh, the temperature feels crisp, the playing surface looks spotless and is shimmering slightly in the low, bright sunlight, so much so that the Tottenham goalkeeper Lize Kop has her arm raised to her forehead to try and shield her eyes from the sunshine. There is just the faintest ripple of wind. It’s almost like something from a painting.
GOAL! Manchester City 1-0 Tottenham (Khadija Shaw, 10)
Shaw strikes for City!
Rose wins the ball high up the pitch before passing to Shaw, who is left in plenty of space in the box. The striker then has plenty of time to slide the ball home.
Shaw is now just one goal away from equalling the WSL all-time top goalscoring record. Can she do it today?
Manchester City 0-0 Tottenham: Blakstad receives a yellow card for pulling Fujino back just outside the box. Manchester City have a free kick but nothing comes of it.
Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United: What a start that is for Birmingham. There is still a long way to go, however, and they have struggled with retaining a lead at times this season.
GOAL! Birmingham 1-0 Manchester United (Lee Geum-min, 4)
Lee fires Birmingham into an early lead!
Her initial shot is blocked, but she is first to the volley and fires the ball into the bottom-left corner.
Birmingham 0-0 Manchester United: The visitors are first to have an attempt at goal as a corner is sent into the box. However, Zigiotti heads it over the crossbar.
Kick-off
Here we go! Both games are under way.
Olivia Holdt was set to start for Tottenham this afternoon, but she has been forced to withdraw from the squad due to illness. The attacking midfielder was visibly emotional while speaking to Martin Ho during the warm-up, she is understandably devastated about not being able to play.
Matilda Vinberg has stepped in to replace her.

Subs: Baggaley, Harris, Rastocle, Magill, Amano, Holloway, Sarri, Molendo-Payne, Janny.

items.text:
Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games
- Published
Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge.
The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.
Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.
Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.
The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.
The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.
Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table.
"We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website., external
"As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.
"The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly."
Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches.
His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game.
But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets.
Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge.
Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games.
On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme".

items.title: Bruno Fernandes reveals talks over new Manchester United contract are on hold
items.summary:
Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but discussions have been put on hold as the club focus on turning around their terrible start to the season.
Fernandes’s current deal expires at the end of this campaign, although United hold an option to extend th
items.text:
Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but discussions have been put on hold as the club focus on turning around their terrible start to the season.
Fernandes’s current deal expires at the end of this campaign, although United hold an option to extend their captain’s contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach an agreement on fresh terms.
“The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on,” Fernandes told Sky Sports in an interview published on Sunday.
“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations,” Fernandes added. “The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.“
The 32-year-old’s future is still up in the air after it was revealed he turned down a second contract offer from the club. Fernandes’s form has dropped off this season, his goal and assist in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa providing his first goal involvements in the league since scoring a hat-trick against Ipswich in August.
The Portugal international also hit back at rumours he had demanded more money and a longer deal, saying his priority was to remain at Old Trafford and help restore the club’s fortunes.
“I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United,” Fernandes said. “I could have been in a place that’s much warmer than Manchester.”
United are second-bottom of the Premier League standings having won only one of their opening 10 league matches – their worst start to a season in 40 years. Their new head coach, Mauricio Pochettino, will take charge of his first game when United face fifth-placed Liverpool on Sunday. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager was appointed after Michael Carrick was sacked this month.
